newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts reel from Philips Q3 shock.
newsitem.headline: Analysts reel from Philips Q3 shock.

text.p: Dutch electronics giant Philips Electronics NV's shock announcement on Thursday of sharply lower than expected third quarter net and more massive restructuring charges left analysts reeling.
"It's even worse than expected," said Daan Muusers of Wesselius Effectenbank.

Philips earlier announced third quarter ordinary net plunged 77 percent to 123 million guilders ($72.2 million) from a year-earlier 539 million. Analysts had been forecasting between 240 and 360 million guilders.
"The fact that they are setting a further one billion guilders aside for restructuring (in the fourth quarter) stresses the bad shape the company is in," Muusers added.
But ING Barings' Eric de Graaf was more upbeat, saying that despite the initial shock of the bottom line figure things were not as bad as they might seem.
"We had effectively written off 1996 anyway," he said. "Taking a one billion charge in the fourth quarter will enable Philips to start next year with a clean slate."
He said the fall in income at software and services reflected one-off charges for the integration of Origin and BSO.
Results at components and semiconductors, in past years one of Philips' major cash cows, were also likely pressured by start-up costs at its Nijmegen plant, De Graaf said.
"On the other hand, consumer products seems to be bottoming out," he said.

De Graaf said he was encouraged by recently-installed chairman Cor Boonstra's pledge to tackle the company's problems more aggressively. "Boonstra has stated unambiguously that if activities are not performing well they will be sold or closed down...I am very positive about that."
He said ING Barings was recommending Philips as a buy, based on performance in years to come, and would keep it as such for the time being.
Ad van der Laar of Bank Labouchere was more sceptical on Boonstra's performance targets, although he stressed he was awaiting further details from a corporate briefing for analysts.
"They (the targets) are very ambitious, to say the least," Van der Laar said. "But what else can Boonstra say?"

Boonstra told a news conference earlier the company was targeting sustainable double-digit growth in income from operations during the course of 1997. He said return on net assets (RONA) should rise to 24 percent next year from 8.4 now.
Van der Laar said Bank Labouchere currently had the stock on a Hold recommendation, but added: "For me it's a trading stock."
"There are stocks with a lower risk profile," agreed ING Barings' De Graaf.
By 1115 GMT Philips shares were 0.40 higher at 57.00 guilders, well above an earlier low of 53.00 guilders hit soon after the results were released.
